chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Abu Basir said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that it be said to the female slaves, 'O so-and-so's daughter,' and he said, 'For every people, there is a marriage/custom.'

key_terms.لِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ نِكَاحٌ: For every people, there is a marriage/custom
key_terms.يَا بِنْتَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا: O so-and-so's daughter (a specific form of address)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid regarding how to address female slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on preserving the dignity of female slaves by prohibiting the patronymic address 'O so-and-so's daughter,' which may have implied a specific social hierarchy or ownership status. The accompanying maxim 'for every people, marriage' (li-kulli qawm nikah) reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *urf* (custom), indicating that marital customs and social norms are adaptable to the specific cultural context of different communities, provided they do not contradict Sharia principles.
